rows.what the ink shows: The cancellation crosses almost the entire middle of the short word. An initial tall bent stroke, a detached dark dot above the middle, and the final crossed stem survive; the obscured middle does not securely establish Cet.

The i dot, tall crossed t and acute mark secure dualité; the final separated word has the tall t and paired l strokes of naturelle. Between them, x1330–1418 is a distinct horizontally cancelled group whose letters and word count cannot be recovered; the earlier compressed groups remain uncertain.

A tall loop at the left and a final upright with a lower hook remain above and below the horizontal cancellation. That cancellation completely covers the intervening low letters, including the proposed oi, so the four-letter reading remains uncertain.

After the comma, cela has a low initial stroke followed by the taller l; comme and on form separate low groups. Sait has the separated i dot and final raised t, and bien starts with the tall looped b and ends before the closing parenthesis.

The coefficient after the first summation has a closed upper loop joined to a long descending stem, with a separate small i below and to the right. This loop-and-descender shape supports rho rather than the two sloping strokes of lambda.
Between the second summation and barred e, a distinct looped rho descends below the baseline; its small i is written at lower right with a separated dot. The coefficient is visibly present.
Immediately after F to E, the word has a low connected initial so group, a short i trace, and a tall terminal t whose cross stroke runs rightward. A comma follows before le v.

The left w and two equality strokes are followed by overlapping crossed and looped ink, then two distinct baseline v bowls and a raised star at the right. Only the preceding fragment and its textual status remain unresolved; the two v letters and terminal star are secure.

Both trace initials and the equality survive. The left baseline cluster is merged by a thick cancellation, preventing separate identification of the three letters or raised star; on the right the last glyph has the two connected low bowls of w, with an uncertain preceding small cup and no distinguishable raised star.
Despite the horizontal cancellation, the initial L stem, opening parenthesis, two capital E forms separated by a low comma, and closing parenthesis remain visible.
The lower replacement line shows u, the membership sign, a capital E with a separate raised prime, a closed tensor circle with crossing strokes, and a final capital E at the page edge.

A heavy nearly horizontal strike obscures the word bodies, while several isolated upright and descending remnants survive above and below it. The intersecting broad cancellation curves prevent a defensible three-word reading.

The initial w is a clear double scoop. The following short horizontal strokes and rounded letter remnants are interrupted by a cancellation curve, and the material at the right occupies two baselines; neither the verb nor the proposed encore un op. sequence can be separated securely.
Under the short cancellation after w, a small initial e/s body leads to the taller crossed t stem and low exit stroke; the inserted =Vv is distinctly above it.

After the canceled est ends, a clear gap leads directly to the first descending p of propriété; there is no intervening la. A second p descender and the final tall t with accented e establish the single word before de v.

The initial descending p and compressed ré carry a visible acute accent; the middle strokes are closely joined. The ending has a tall looped t-like stroke followed by an independent open rounded e, supporting précédente rather than précédent.
A heavy rising horizontal cancellation covers almost the full word; only a short dark left hook and low central remnants remain, insufficient to separate letters.
The small initial open curved stroke is followed by a low angular a and an extended horizontal r ending; there is no tall stem within the word.
An open e and crossed x precede short upright strokes; the reduced middle continues into a long low run, then a dotted i and clearly crossed final t.

The underlined baseline form begins with a compact s and has tightly joined tall strokes for the contracted t/b/l group, ending in an open e; no separate a appears. The thinner inserted stable sits above it.

The large initial M and following e-like loop are clear, followed by a small horizontal stroke and tall h-like stroke. A distinct dot and low terminal loop make an abbreviated Méth. form a concrete competitor to full Méthode; the thin méthode above does not settle the original baseline letters.

Above the baseline L are three separate components: a curved left parenthesis, a capped descending 2, and a curved right parenthesis. The central numeral matches the small unparenthesized 2 over L in the next line.
